title: An enzyme with and without inhibitor P

stimulus.title: An enzyme with and without inhibitor P
stimulus.html:
Researchers measured the initial rate of a human enzyme at six substrate concentrations, with no inhibitor and with 2 mM of inhibitor P, at 37 °C and pH 7.4. The same amount of enzyme was used in every trial.

Initial reaction rate (µmol of product per minute)
Substrate concentration (mM)No inhibitorWith inhibitor P

266.728.6
583.350.0
1090.966.7
5098.090.9

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe how the effect of inhibitor P changes as substrate concentration increases.

rubric.point: Describes that P lowers the rate strongly at low substrate concentration and less and less as substrate rises, until the inhibited rate is close to the uninhibited rate at 50 mM.
accept: the inhibitor's effect gets smaller as substrate increases
at 0.5 mM P cuts the rate to about a quarter, at 50 mM to about 93%

parts.sample: At low substrate P has a large effect: at 0.5 mM the rate falls from 33.3 to 9.1. As substrate increases the effect shrinks, and at 50 mM the inhibited rate (90.9) is close to the uninhibited rate (98.0).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the rate with inhibitor P at 2 mM substrate as a percentage of the rate with no inhibitor at the same concentration.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Identify whether P is a competitive or a noncompetitive inhibitor, and support your answer with evidence from the data.

rubric.point: Identifies P as competitive, citing that high substrate overcomes it so the rate approaches the uninhibited maximum (90.9 against 98.0 at 50 mM).
accept: competitive, because at high substrate the inhibited rate nearly reaches the uninhibited rate

parts.sample: P is a competitive inhibitor. At 50 mM substrate the rate with P (90.9) is nearly the same as without it (98.0), so enough substrate outcompetes P for the active site and the same maximum is approached. A noncompetitive inhibitor would keep the maximum rate lower however much substrate was added.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A second inhibitor, R, binds the enzyme at an allosteric site. Predict the rate at 50 mM substrate with R present compared with the rate without any inhibitor, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts a rate clearly below 98.0 even at 50 mM, because R changes the enzyme's shape at a site the substrate does not compete for, so extra substrate cannot restore the maximum.
accept: lower than 98.0 because a noncompetitive inhibitor lowers the maximum rate
the rate stays well below the uninhibited rate since substrate cannot displace an inhibitor at an allosteric site

parts.sample: The rate at 50 mM will stay well below 98.0. R binds an allosteric site and changes the shape of the active site, so the enzymes it binds work poorly. Because R does not compete with the substrate for the active site, adding more substrate cannot reverse its effect, so the maximum rate is lowered.
